results.question: What was our revenue in each month?

results.question: Which month had the highest revenue, and how much was it?

results.question: Which product type sells the most units?

results.question: Which day of the week do we get the most orders, and how many?

results.question: At the peak hour of the day (Sydney time), how many online orders do we get in total?
results.sql: SELECT peak_hour.hour_of_day AS hour_of_day, count(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders o JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney'))::integer AS hour_of_day) peak_hour WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND l.type = 'online' GROUP BY peak_hour.hour_of_day ORDER BY count(o.order_id) DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Your peak hour for online orders is 8:00 PM Sydney time, with a total of 1,232 orders placed across the entire data period from October 2025 to September 2026. This count excludes any voided orders.

results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - sum(v.cost * l.quantity), 2) AS gross_profit, round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 2) AS total_revenue_ex_gst, round(((sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - sum(v.cost * l.quantity)) / nullif(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 0)) * 100, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_percent FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin for the period is 58.32 percent, generating $1,584,502.69 in gross profit from $2,716,823.41 in revenue. This calculation assumes revenue is ex-GST after discounts and subtracts total unit costs, while excluding any product variants that had missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Interpreting gross profit margin across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is taken ex-GST (divided by 1.1) after discounts, minus total unit costs. Variants with NULL costs are excluded.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - (v.cost * l.quantity)) AS gross_profit, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v USING (product_id) JOIN order_lines l USING (variant_id) JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top 5 products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit at $165,884.48 (4,043 units sold), Shirt Dress at $130,441.22 (1,492 units), Straw Hat at $108,854.01 (3,619 units), High-Rise Jeans at $104,531.12 (1,295 units), and Wool Coat at $89,912.11 (828 units). This covers the full period from October 2025 to September 2026. These figures exclude product variants where the cost was missing, and group products by their title.
results.assumptions: Assumed gross profit as (revenue ex-GST) minus (cost ex-GST). Excluded variants where cost is NULL. Evaluated over the full data period (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026). Products grouped by title.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.total) - COALESCE(SUM(r.amount), 0), 2) AS net_revenue, ROUND(SUM(o.total), 2) AS gross_revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(r.amount), 0), 2) AS total_refunds FROM orders o LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds is $3,205,298.79 for the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. This was calculated by subtracting $116,631.92 in total refunds from a gross revenue of $3,321,930.71. This calculation excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Interpreting net revenue as total order revenue (excluding voided orders) minus total refund amounts across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?

results.answer: 5.7% of your orders had a refund. This is based on all orders and refunds recorded between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026, assuming voided orders were excluded from the total count.

results.question: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many?

results.answer: The product with the most units refunded is the One-Piece Swimsuit, with 165 units refunded. This data excludes voided orders based on their financial status.

results.question: How many different customers have placed an order?

results.question: What percentage of orders were placed by guests with no customer account?
results.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / count(*), 2) AS percentage_guest_orders, sum(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS guest_order_count, count(*) AS total_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Guests with no customer account placed 22.47% of all orders, totaling 3,896 guest orders out of 17,340 total orders between October 2025 and September 2026. This calculation includes all non-voided orders across the entire data period.

results.answer: Your gross revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 in July, $282,129.97 in August, and $278,068.87 in September 2026. This assumes "last 3 months" refers to the final three months of available data up to September 30, 2026, and includes all non-voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?

results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units across the entire period are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These totals exclude any voided orders based on the data provided for October 2025 through September 2026.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS average_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation looks at the calendar days between when an order and its refund were created, focusing only on non-voided orders.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as the average number of calendar days between order creation (orders.created_at) and refund creation (refunds.created_at) for all non-voided orders.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Camel was your top-selling colour in winter, with 1,050 units sold. This total is based on non-voided orders between June 1 and August 31, 2026, using Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Winter 2026 is defined as June 1 to August 31, 2026, based on Australia/Sydney time. Units sold are summed from non-voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, round(sum(o.total), 2) AS gross_revenue, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more money than weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 across 6,187 orders on weekends. These figures cover all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, using Sydney local time to separate the days.
results.assumptions: Interpreting revenue as gross revenue (orders.total) for non-voided orders across the entire date range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), converting timestamps to Australia/Sydney time to determine weekends (Saturday and Sunday) versus weekdays.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(l.quantity) DESC) AS rnk FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines l ON v.variant_id = l.variant_id JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title AS best_selling_product, units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY product_type;
results.answer: The best-selling products by total units sold across each product type for the period of October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2025, are the Straw Hat for accessories with 3,619 units, the Shirt Dress for dresses with 1,492 units, the Merino Crew Jumper for knitwear with 526 units, and the Wool Coat for outerwear with 828 units. Additionally, the High-Rise Jeans led pants with 1,295 units, the Linen Wrap Skirt led skirts with 1,804 units, the One-Piece Swimsuit led swimwear with 4,043 units, and the Ribbed Tank led tops with 1,395 units. These results are based on non-voided orders and assume product types were accurately categorized.
results.assumptions: Interpreting best-selling by total units sold across all non-voided orders for the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Product types are normalized to lowercase.
